description: The Tobacco Enforcement Operations unit is responsible for regulating tobacco retailers to ensure compliance with all applicable laws, including proper permitting and prohibitions against sales to minors. Through undercover minor decoy compliance checks, retailer education, and outreach, the unit enforces restrictions on unlawful sales, including the prohibition of flavored tobacco products that are known to appeal to youth. While the program does not provide direct services to youth, the objective behind enforcement activities is the protection of youth from the harms of tobacco-use and addiction.

The Los Angeles City Attorney's Homeless Engagement and Response Team (H.E.A.R.T.) administers the Los Angeles County Homeless Court Program.  HEART  helps unhoused individuals or individuals at risk of experiencing homelessness clear traffic and pedestrian tickets by engaging in services instead of paying expensive fines and fees.  HEART accepts direct referrals from approved service providers, including providers that work directly with youth (18+), to provide assistance with ticket clearance.  HEART also attends homeless youth record clearance events to connect youth with services and remove barriers to housing, education, and employment.

description: TAY Diversion is a post-filing, in-court diversion program for young adults aged 18-25. Upon completion of diversion, the participant's case is dismissed.

program: Gang Reduction and Youth Development (GRYD) program
description: The Gang Reduction and Youth Development (GRYD) program, operated by the City of Los Angeles Mayor’s Office, is a comprehensive initiative aimed at preventing and reducing gang involvement and violence among youth and young adults ages 10 to 25. Established in 2007, GRYD provides prevention and intervention services across 23 designated zones, focusing on individualized case management, family support, reentry services, and community engagement. The program also includes citywide initiatives like Summer Night Lights to create safe spaces and positive alternatives during peak violence hours. GRYD partners with community-based organizations, city departments, and academic institutions to deliver services, track progress, and improve outcomes through research and evaluation.

description:
Clean LA is a one-year employment program for job-seeking Angelenos who would like to help clean and green the City of Los Angeles as a pathway to a full-time career. 

Participants in the CleanLA program conduct cleaning services along the public right-of-way to beautify neighborhoods in Los Angeles. After completing 1920 hours and other program requirements, participants will be provided an opportunity to be hired with the City of Los Angeles. Participants are initially hired by the City as exempt Vocational Workers in which they receive on-the-job training for the first six months. Successful participants then transition to the Maintenance Assistant civil service classification for a six-month probational period, followed by a Charter Section 1014 transfer to Maintenance Laborer.

description:
Works in partnership with the LA Black Workers Center that provides underserved and low-income communities direct access to public sector employment through intentional recruitment, hiring, training, and mentorship that ensures quality careers for Black workers.

Participants are further mentored to promote into journey-level classifications such as Tree Surgeon, Truck Operator, and Heavy Duty Truck Operator.
